newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania looks into unrepatriated export earnings.
newsitem.headline: Romania looks into unrepatriated export earnings.

text.p: Romania's government on Friday urged Finance Ministry and central bank controls into the reasons behind exporters' failure to repatriate some $2.8 billion worth of export earnings in the past few years.

"A cabinet meeting decided that the Finance Ministry and National Bank (BNR) bodies across the country should start checking on repatriation of export earnings by companies," a government statement said.
The $2.8 billion figure is roughly equal to total direct foreign investments in Romania in seven years and it exceeds the country's end-1996 current account deficit.
Romanian law sets definite earnings repatriation terms only for a limited number of exports -- similar to those abroad.
A central bank official said the repatriation term for earnings from crude oil exports was of 180 days, while that of concerete iron was 360 days.

"If companies fail to repatriate their earnings within the interval, the BNR -- which centralises all hard currency earning statements -- notifies the Finance Ministry which starts controls," the official said.
Finance Ministry officials were not immediately available for comment.
